answer: The farm's purse empties long before its list of names does. The price of trying is a toll of 12 credits, collected in coin before the name is written down, paid up front for every single name, while the fable stays small. To join, a name must pass Valued groom of the chamber stable charter, which works because a charter grooms file after chamber hearings. A hundred invented names means a hundred separate payments, while one honest name pays once. One prism, one entry. The ridge is checked, not assumed.
